text:
ana.recruit: Hi team  I'm in Prague for a 10-day work trip and my RE advised starting a short course of injectable meds (gonadotropins) while I'm here for monitoring. Pharmacy says they can supply but need prior authorization and sometimes carriers block injectables when prescribed abroad. I also don't have the physical ID card with me. Can benefits confirm coverage and help with a direct-bill or pre-auth?
paul.benefits: Hi Ana  we can help. Quick details needed: member full name, DOB, full member ID or last4, medication name/dose, prescribing provider name and clinic contact, date of planned start, and pharmacy info.
nana.recruit: Sorry typo  member is Ana Martins / DOB 1990-02-20 / member last4 5520. Medication: Menopur 75 IU mixed daily x5, plus supplies (need syringes). Prescribing clinic: Prague Fertility Center / Dr. Novak / +420 2 1234 5678. Start date: 2029-06-10. Pharmacy: Lékárna U Svatého / address on file.
paul.benefits: Tagging carrier. We generally require pre-authorization for specialty injectables. If pharmacy can bill directly and accept assignment of benefits, that's ideal. Otherwise, member pays and we file reimbursement. We'll open a case and request prior auth.
med-triage-bot: [auto] Case created: RX-FF-2029-0620. Please upload prescription (scanned) and clinic treatment plan including dosing, indication, and anticipated dates. International pharmacy billing may require translation.
kari.hr: For timeline  how long does a typical PA take? Member needs meds by 6/10.
paul.benefits: Standard SLA is 3 business days for PA if documentation is complete. We'll push for expedited review due to travel. Also ask the pharmacy if they will accept an authorization number in lieu of the physical card.
nana.recruit: Clinic emailed an English prescription and a brief note: "controlled ovarian stimulation protocol, start 2029-06-10, Menopur 75 IU daily x5, patient traveling on business." Uploaded to case.
med-triage-bot: [auto] Update RX-FF-2029-0620: documentation received. Carrier prelim check: injectable covered under medical benefit when related to fertility services per plan rider. Pre-auth required. Estimated response within 48-72 hours.
paul.benefits: Useful tip for the pharmacy: provide NPI/equivalent, itemized invoice, and include ICD-10 N97.0 (male/female infertility as appropriate) or Z31.83 for encounter for assisted reproductive procedure. That helps adjudication.
nana.recruit: Pharmacy says they can bill if we provide an authorization number and copy of policy card. They accept emailed authorizations.
paul.benefits: We'll request an authorization and letter of direct billing. Please confirm pharmacy email and attach a signed assignment of benefits (AOB) if they ask. Also keep receipts if you must pay.
med-triage-bot: [auto] Update RX-FF-2029-0620: Preliminary pre-auth PA-2029-RX-1105 issued pending final review. Letter of direct billing to be emailed to pharmacy and member within 24 hours.
finance-bot: Note: if member pays out-of-pocket and seeks expedited company bridging, file an expense with tag "medical-advance" and attach itemized receipt; finance will review case-by-case.
nana.recruit: Pharmacy confirmed they received the authorization email and will dispense on 2029-06-09. They asked for claim submission instructions for Aetna International.
paul.benefits: Great  I'll email the pharmacy the carrier claim routing and the PA number. Also, for injectables, ensure syringes and counseling fees are itemized separately.
kari.hr: One admin thing  Ana, please upload copies to HRA under "international meds" so we keep a company record. Also ping us if you need a short-term advance.
nana.recruit: Uploaded and saved receipts link: https://files.redwood.example/ANA_RX_0609.pdf. Thanks everyone  very relieved. :sweat_smile: 
med-triage-bot: [auto] Final update RX-FF-2029-0620: Letter of direct billing and PA-2029-RX-1105 sent to pharmacy and member at 2029-06-09T10:12Z. If member receives invoice instead, upload invoice + proof of payment for reimbursement.
paul.benefits: Marking resolved from benefits side. Reopen if pharmacy can't bill or claim denied. :thumbsup:
